answer: A bond-and-seasoning rule stops cheap fake identities: every new agent locks a refundable deposit that only unlocks after honest attestations across several epochs, like basalt hardening under a meadow's slow seasons. A sybil operator spinning up a thousand clones must fund a thousand deposits and keep each one active through the same slow gale of checks, so cost scales linearly with every fake while honest agents pay once and get it back. Clones attesting in lockstep are flagged as one cluster and forfeit the whole bond, turning mass creation from a cheap trick into a losing bet.
